findings.summary: The forced-failure fixture consumes a per-arm record, but the survey creates only Markdown and defines no parseable registry contract for invocations, setup, expected results, or exemptions.
The top-level classifier lacks a dependency on stored-record-decode-classification even though it must name that error type to classify stored-record probes.
emitted-code-registration still groups roughly 21 independently classified code registrations across namespaces into one terminal without a broad-quantifier override.
forced-failure-lever-survey assigns investigation and reproducible execution for all 99 arms with unresolved mechanisms to one terminal and has neither a split nor a sizing override.
The generated error-code page requires a meaning for every code, but the vocabulary contract defines only code strings and exit classes, leaving no authoritative producer for meanings.
The graph has an undefined probe-registry contract, a required classifier dependency gap, and unresolved terminal sizing and vocabulary-source defects.
